APP_PROJECT := WorkroomApp.xcodeproj
APP_NAME    := Workroom Dev
APP_BUNDLE  := DerivedData/Build/Products/Debug/$(APP_NAME).app
APP_XCODEBUILD := xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomApp -configuration Debug \
  -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages

# Extra xcodebuild build-setting overrides, appended to app-build/app-test. Empty locally so
# ⌘R-style automatic signing is used; CI sets this to ad-hoc / no-team signing because hosted
# runners have no signing cert or DEVELOPMENT_TEAM (e.g.
# `make app-test APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="`).
APP_SIGN_FLAGS ?=

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-test. Parallel execution by default: the suite is dominated by a
# few slow integration classes (Markdown WebView renders, real git/jj repos), so spreading classes
# across worker processes cuts the run ~40% (48s -> ~29s). Each worker gets its own host-app process
# but they share one UserDefaults domain, so a test mutating a `Defaults` key another class reads
# would race — override with `make app-test APP_TEST_FLAGS=` to bisect a suspected parallel-only
# failure. Test dirs are already UUID-scoped under NSTemporaryDirectory, so those don't collide.
APP_TEST_FLAGS ?= -parallel-testing-enabled YES

# The Rust VCS core (jj-lib via UniFFI) the app links, built into the local WrVcs SwiftPM package
# (vcs/swift/WrVcs). Must run before xcodegen so the package's xcframework + generated Swift exist.
# arm64 by default; release/distribution sets VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal (needs rustup stable >=
# 1.93 + both darwin targets, and `protoc` on PATH for jj-lib's build).
VCS_APPLE_FLAGS ?=
app-vcs: ## Build the Rust VCS core (xcframework + Swift bindings) the app links
	vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh $(VCS_APPLE_FLAGS)

app-run: app-build ## Build (Debug) and launch the dev app, replacing any running dev instance
	cd macapp || exit 1; \
	pkill -x "$(APP_NAME)" 2>/dev/null || true; \
	i=0; \
	while pgrep -x "$(APP_NAME)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ $$i -lt 40 ]; do \
	  sleep 0.2; i=$$((i + 1)); \
	done; \
	echo "Launching $(APP_BUNDLE)"; \
	open "$(APP_BUNDLE)"

app-build: app-vcs ## Build the app (Debug)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) build $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test: app-vcs ## Run the app's unit tests
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_TEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-uitest: app-vcs ## Run the app's UI tests (XCUITest — needs a real GUI login session, not headless)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test-supervisor: ## Run the run-command supervisor PTY integration test (real shell + fake server)
	python3 macapp/Tests/run-supervisor/test_supervisor.py

app-generate: app-vcs ## Force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate

app-format: ## Format Swift sources in place (swift-format)
	cd macapp && xcrun swift-format format --in-place --parallel --recursive WorkroomApp WorkroomAppTests WorkroomAppUITests

content.text:
Verdict first: **no**. macOS XCUITest cannot be confined to a display. Displays aren't sessions — one login session has one WindowServer, one cursor, one key-focus. XCUITest synthesizes real HID events into that session and `app.activate()`/`typeKey` steal frontmost regardless of where the window sits. No `Xvfb` equivalent, no `-destination` display selector.

What actually isolates: a **second GUI session** — separate macOS VM, or a second Mac. Everything else is damage reduction.

Repo facts found:
- `Makefile:84` `app-uitest` runs the whole `WorkroomAppUITests` scheme, ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS` (matches your known gotcha — no easy `-only-testing:` scoping).
- No workflow in `.github/workflows/` runs UI tests. Full suite only ever runs on your laptop.
- Tests hammer global input: `app.typeKey("t", .command)`, `app.activate()`, ⌘, ⌘W across 26 classes.

Cheap wins exist (scope flag pass-through, offload full suite to CI runner). True isolation costs setup: Tart/VirtualBuddy macOS guest needs Xcode + rustup + protoc + xcodegen inside it (`app-uitest` depends on `app-vcs`), or a build-on-host / `test-without-building`-in-guest split.

questions.question: Which isolation route should the plan target?

options.label: CI offload + local scoping (Recommended)
options.description: Add a UI-test workflow on a GitHub macOS runner for the full suite, plus a Makefile flag pass-through so local runs are one scoped class/method. Cheapest, no new hardware, laptop hijack shrinks from ~26 classes to seconds. Does NOT eliminate hijack for local runs.

options.label: macOS VM runner (Tart/VirtualBuddy)
options.description: True isolation: VM window lives on the external monitor, host input untouched. Costs 60-90GB image + Xcode/rustup/protoc/xcodegen in guest (or build-on-host + test-without-building in guest). Risk: libghostty Metal rendering under paravirtualized GPU.

options.label: Second Mac as remote runner
options.description: Cleanest isolation if you have spare hardware. ssh in, run make app-uitest on its own logged-in GUI session. Needs auto-login + full toolchain on that Mac.

options.label: All three, phased
options.description: Ship scoping + CI first, then stand up the VM as the long-term local isolation.

questions.question: Spare Mac available as a runner?

options.label: No spare Mac
options.description: Rules out the remote-runner route; VM or CI only.

options.label: Yes, but rarely on
options.description: Viable but unreliable — plan should not depend on it.
